title: Some People Only Respond to Thunder
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece addresses the frustrating case of team members who receive the same feedback repeatedly without ever acting on it, and argues that some people genuinely require a more forceful delivery, what the author calls 'thunder', before feedback registers at all. Importantly, the piece clarifies that thunder is about emphasis and intensity, not volume or yelling, offering a list of concrete tactics. Citing Mark Twain's line that 'it is lightning that does the work,' the piece frames thunder as the delivery mechanism that clears the way for the substantive feedback to land.
points: Some team members consistently fail to register repeated feedback, not out of disagreement but because they don't perceive it as significant.
'Thunder' is explicitly distinguished from yelling, it's about emphasis and unmistakable seriousness of delivery.
The piece offers concrete thunder tactics: unusual meeting locations or times, circulating written feedback from multiple colleagues, requiring a reflection day.
Using Twain's line that 'lightning does the work,' the piece frames thunder as merely the delivery mechanism.
quotes: Team members who repetitively receive the same feedback but don’t acknowledge or act on it create a huge leadership challenge.

Regrettably, some people only respond to thunder. Thunder can be loud, highly expressive, firm, or insistent. What makes it thunder is the manner in which the feedback is emphasized, not the volume of the leader.
Sharing written and candid feedback from a host of colleagues and asking them to read it out loud
Good leaders reserve the thunder of yelling for fires. There are many other more effective ways to create thunder.
For those hard-to-reach team members, the best leaders produce the thunder (emphasis) and the lightning (feedback) to get the job done.
